claims.text: The magnetocaloric response of as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys is governed by nano-twins and stacking faults.
Hysteresis in as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys is governed by nano-twins and stacking faults.
Nano-twins and stacking faults form during deformation.
Alloy composition influences the formation of nano-twins and stacking faults.
Longitudinal spin fluctuations influence the formation of nano-twins and stacking faults.
Deformation can be used to introduce controlled populations of nano-twins and stacking faults.
The proposed effects apply during low-applied-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Introducing nano-twins and stacking faults will enhance the magnetocaloric response relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Introducing nano-twins and stacking faults will reduce hysteresis relative to the as-deposited baseline.
The predictions hold across FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys having varying Fe, Mn, Ni, Ge, and Si concentrations.
The exact relationship among longitudinal spin fluctuations, nano-twins, stacking faults, magnetocaloric response, and hysteresis is uncertain.
Failure of controlled defect introduction to enhance magnetocaloric response and reduce hysteresis would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis attributes behavior in the as-deposited state to defects formed during deformation, while the specified deformation is a post-deposition intervention. It does not explain how deformation-generated defects govern the undeformed as-deposited baseline.
